title: Microbilling accumulation from batch-window rounding in multi-region fanout
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
A set of customers reported steady, small monthly overcharges (0.5%–2% of expected bill) that accumulated over several billing cycles. The issue only appears for tenants that receive a large number of very small requests (average request < 250 tokens) that are fan‑out routed across multiple regions (hosted + dedicated linkbacks).

Observed behavior:
- Token accounting on ingest occasionally rounds up fractional token-attribution during batch-window close. Multiple ingress shards handling the same logical window applied independent rounding before aggregation, resulting in net positive rounding bias.
- The bias is tiny per-request (typically 1–3 tokens), but for tenants with high QPS of small requests it summed to material deltas across a month.
- Bias amplified when requests triggered cross-region fallback (fanout) leading to duplicated partial attributions that the aggregator incorrectly merged instead of deduplicating.

How we discovered it:
- Triggered by two customer escalations (one enterprise and one mid-market) that had unexplained monthly deltas.
- Onboarding billing engineer correlated anomalies to request size distribution and multi-region routing.
- Dashboard (billing/agg/token-attribution) showed persistent small positive skew coincident with region failover windows and high small-request traffic.

Root cause (summary):
1) Batch-window rounding: Per-shard aggregator applied rounding to fractional token attributions before emitting per-window metrics. Aggregators used float->int conversion with round-to-nearest which created a small positive bias when several partial attributions for the same logical request were later combined.
2) Fanout duplication: During multi-region routing and fallback, certain requests were sent to multiple backends (primary + fallback). In some edge cases the idempotency token emitted by the load balancer did not reach all shards due to transient header truncation; the aggregator could not deduplicate those partial attributions and kept both rounded-up counts.
3) Late-window correction missing: There's no correction pass that reconciles per-request attribution against the authoritative ingress ledger once late packets arrive.

Immediate mitigation performed (rolled out within 24h):
- Disabled pre-aggregation rounding at each shard; shards now emit high-precision counts (integer micro-token units) and final rounding happens in the global aggregator.
- Temporarily tightened fanout path (3-hr config) to avoid sending redundant requests in fallback windows for affected customers.
- Issued an interim bill-credit for the two reporting customers while we investigate scope.

Fix implemented (hotfix):
- Global aggregation updated to: (a) perform deterministic sum of micro-token units, (b) apply round-half-to-even at final invoice boundary to eliminate systematic positive bias, (c) deduplicate using the idempotency token and a short-lived per-window dedupe cache.
- Ingress LB and header propagation fixed to ensure idempotency token consistently reaches all shards (PR linked).

Fallbacks and reconciliation plan:
- Run backfill reconciliation across the last 6 months for tenants with high small-request ratios. We have a backfill script that replays ingress ledger and produces corrected monthly deltas for review.
- Prepare automated credits pipeline (manual review first, automated in release-2) to apply corrections and notify customers via billing.

Telemetry and alerts added:
- New metric: window-rounding-skew (per-tenant, per-region). Alert if >0.2% over 6h window.
- New SLO: dedupe hit rate for idempotency tokens; alert on drop below 99.9%.

Next steps / follow-ups:
- Expand reconciliation to Dedicated and Private customers (some private deployments delayed due to KMS masking of headers; coordination with SRE and Private infra needed).
- Add an end-to-end test harness that simulates high small-request QPS with fanout to capture rounding/dedup edgecases.
- Postmortem doc with customer communication templates and SLA credit calculations.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/METER/Microbilling+rounding+incident
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/15823
- Backfill script repo & runbook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering-tools/tree/main/backfills/micro-rounding
- Alert runbook: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OPS/Window+rounding+alerts

Business impact estimate:
- Affected tenants: ~27 (mix of hosted and dedicated), potential credit exposure ~$42k MRR equivalent if extrapolated over 6 months before detection. Immediate known impact limited to three high-volume tenants; broader set flagged for reconciliation.

comments: 2026-03-01: Ticket opened after customer escalation from AcmeFin and build-up of similar anomalies in hosted customers. Ava ran initial aggregation queries and validated skew on the billing dashboard.
2026-03-02: Hotfix branch created; disabled per-shard rounding and deployed to a small canary (us-west-2). Observed elimination of positive skew on canary tenants.
2026-03-03: Fanout path tightened for affected customers and temporary bill credits issued pending reconciliation. Billing team requested an estimate for backfill runtime.
2026-03-04: Ingress LB header propagation fix merged (PR #15807). Deployed to staged Dedicated and Private testbeds; idempotency token now visible in all shards.
2026-03-05: Global aggregator changes merged (PR #15823). Running backfill in dry-run mode against last 90 days for validation; job completion ETA 2026-03-12.
2026-03-07: Observability: new metric window-rounding-skew added to dashboards; initial alerts configured. SRE to monitor during next traffic spike window.
2026-03-09: Recon run for top 10 tenants completed; cumulative correction matched interim credits issued. Preparing scheduling to run full 6-month backfill starting 2026-03-11.
2026-03-10: PM and CS aligned on customer comms and SLA credit framework. Next: run full backfill, finalize automated credit pipeline, expand tests.
